After the earlier rounds already rewrote rename/ROB/top, issue_queue/LSU, and commit/dcache/ALU/ID/IF, the untouched liveness-critical pieces are the two caches' external handshake and the predictor. The strongest candidate is icache.sv: an I-cache miss/refill that either retracts mem_req_valid before mem_req_ready, never returns cpu_resp_valid for the outstanding cpu_req_epoch, or leaves cpu_req_ready/idle deasserted forever — that freezes if_stage (and keeps commit_unit.bus_idle low, so the ECALL halt/ halted=1 is never reached). Second is branch_predictor.sv, whose pred_next_pc/pred_taken can be X or stuck when pred_req_valid is low, redirecting IF to an undefined address every cycle (endless flush, zero commits). physical_register_file.sv is the third: undriven/late read ports or a missing complete-write would keep operands unwritten, and the top-level rv32i5.sv cache/external-memory wiring and idle aggregation must be re-checked for the same handshake. No retire PCs are wrong, so this is not a data-path functional bug.
repair_constraints: Never rename ports, modules or files; all interface contracts listed in the plan (rv32i5, icache, dcache, branch_predictor, if_stage, id_stage, rename_unit, physical_register_file, issue_queue, execute_alu, load_store_unit, reorder_buffer, commit_unit) must stay bit-for-bit compatible.

Do not re-apply or re-litigate the already-falsified fixes from attempts 1-3 (rename/ROB/top halt-stop-fetch wiring, issue_queue/load_store_unit, commit_unit/dcache/execute_alu/id_stage/if_stage); any change in those areas must be a revert to the verified baseline, not a new local patch.

The imem/dmem contract is binding: at most one in-flight request per interface, imem_valid/dmem_valid and the address/data/byte-enable must be held stable until the matching ready, imem_addr[1:0]=00 every running cycle, and no in-flight external transaction may be aborted by flush/halt (flush/halt may only suppress the response via the epoch guard).

I-cache must answer every accepted cpu_req_valid exactly once with cpu_resp_valid+cpu_resp_data+cpu_resp_epoch, must never drop an accepted request, and must eventually assert idle; dcache/store path must keep byte-enable merging and must not assemble stale lines on a store miss.

Preserve retirement/halt semantics: exactly one single-cycle dbg_retire_valid per committed instruction, halted=1 and exit_code=x10 appearing on the same cycle after the ECALL commit edge, no cycle with halted=0 and exit_code!=0, and all architectural state frozen once halted=1.

Keep the fetch epoch guard behaviour intact (stale-epoch response discarded, request re-issued) and keep dbg_features/dbg_bp_resolve/dbg_bp_mispredict/dbg_ooo_issue tied to real internal state, not counters or PC patterns.
